title: Quotients by approximating generated ideal sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal S$ a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], and $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal S$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $K$ be a nonempty directed preordered set and $(\mathcal E_k,\eta_{lk})_{k\le l}$ a system of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose compatible module maps $\varepsilon_k:\mathcal E_k\to\mathcal J$ exhibit $\mathcal J$ as their colimit in $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $\mathcal I_k=(\varepsilon_k(\mathcal E_k))\subseteq\mathcal S$ for the generated ideal sheaf and $\mathcal Q_k=\mathcal S/\mathcal I_k$ for the sheaf quotient. Then the natural quotient maps $\mathcal Q_k\to\mathcal S/\mathcal J$ exhibit $\mathcal S/\mathcal J$ as the colimit of the diagram $(\mathcal Q_k)_{k\in K}$ in all sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, and also in their full quasi-coherent subcategory. In particular, on every affine open $U$, these maps identify $\varinjlim_k\mathcal Q_k(U)$ with $\mathcal S(U)/\mathcal J(U)$.

proof.text: Write $j:\mathcal J\hookrightarrow\mathcal S$ and $e_k=j\varepsilon_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b), each $\mathcal I_k=(e_k(\mathcal E_k))$ and $\mathcal Q_k$ is quasi-coherent, and its projection $q_k:\mathcal S\to\mathcal Q_k$ has the universal property for killing $e_k$. Apply the same result with $\mathcal E=\mathcal J$ and $e=j$: the generated ideal is $\mathcal J$ itself, since $\mathcal J$ is an ideal containing its own sections and every ideal containing those sections contains $\mathcal J$. Thus $\mathcal Q=\mathcal S/\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent with projection $q$. Compatibility $e_k=e_l\eta_{lk}$ for $k\le l$ gives $\mathcal I_k\subseteq\mathcal I_l\subseteq\mathcal J$. The quotient universal properties give unique $t_{lk}:\mathcal Q_k\to\mathcal Q_l$ and $r_k:\mathcal Q_k\to\mathcal Q$ with $t_{lk}q_k=q_l$ and $r_kq_k=q$. Their identity, composition and cocone equations follow by uniqueness after precomposing with $q_k$.

source.place: Properties, Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, proof: A = colim Sym(F)/(E_i) since J = colim E_i; used again in Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof, final colimit equality.

proof.text: Let $(\alpha_k:\mathcal Q_k\to\mathcal C)$ be any algebra-sheaf cocone, with $\mathcal C$ arbitrary, as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Set $h_k=\alpha_kq_k$. For $k\le l$, the cocone equation gives $h_k=\alpha_l t_{lk}q_k=\alpha_lq_l=h_l$. Choose $k_0\in K$, possible by nonemptiness, and put $h=h_{k_0}$. For every $k$, choose $l\ge k,k_0$ by directedness. Then $h_k=h_l=h_{k_0}=h$. This uses only the preorder, without antisymmetry.

source.place: Properties, Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, proof: A = colim Sym(F)/(E_i) since J = colim E_i; used again in Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof, final colimit equality.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf], $h$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear on underlying modules: $h(as)=h(a)h(s)=a h(s)$ for local $a\in\mathcal O_X$. For every $k$ we have $(hj)\varepsilon_k=he_k=h_k e_k=\alpha_kq_ke_k=0$. The assumed module colimit and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] imply $hj=0$: $hj$ and the zero module map out of $\mathcal J$ have identical composites with all $\varepsilon_k$, hence are equal. Now [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b), applied with $e=j$, gives a unique algebra map $\bar h:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal C$ satisfying $\bar hq=h$.

source.place: Properties, Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, proof: A = colim Sym(F)/(E_i) since J = colim E_i; used again in Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof, final colimit equality.

proof.text: For each $k$, $(\bar h r_k)q_k=\bar hq=h=\alpha_kq_k$, so uniqueness in the quotient property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b) gives $\bar h r_k=\alpha_k$. If $v:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal C$ is another map with these equations, then $vq=v r_{k_0}q_{k_0}=\alpha_{k_0}q_{k_0}=h$, so the quotient property for $q$ gives $v=\bar h$. This is exactly the colimit property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in all algebra sheaves. Since all $\mathcal Q_k$ and $\mathcal Q$ are quasi-coherent, the identical factorization proves the colimit property in the full quasi-coherent subcategory [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra].

source.place: Properties, Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, proof: A = colim Sym(F)/(E_i) since J = colim E_i; used again in Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof, final colimit equality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit] to the directed diagram $(\mathcal Q_k,t_{lk})$. It supplies an algebra-sheaf colimit $(\mathcal A,c_k)$ and, on every affine open $U$, an isomorphism $\varinjlim_k\mathcal Q_k(U)\to\mathcal A(U)$ induced by $c_{k,U}$. The two colimit properties [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] give the unique isomorphism $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Q$ with $uc_k=r_k$. Explicitly, the universal properties give $u$ and $v:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal A$; the composites $uv$ and $vu$ fix all cocone maps, so uniqueness makes them identities. Evaluation takes its inverse to an inverse of $u_U$, so composing the displayed affine isomorphism with $u_U$ identifies the affine ring colimit with $\mathcal Q(U)$ through the required maps $r_{k,U}$: on each stage, $u_U c_{k,U}=r_{k,U}$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal](b), with $e=j$, identifies $\mathcal Q(U)=\mathcal S(U)/\mathcal J(U)$.

lean.statement: theorem generatedIdealQuotient_colimit {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (hS : X.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra S) (J : X.Modules) (hJ : J.IsQuasicoherent) (j : J ⟶ S.toModule) (L : ∀ U : X.Opens, Ideal (S.right.obj.obj (op U))) (hj : ∀ U : X.Opens, Function.Injective (j.app U) ∧ Set.range (j.app U) = (L U : Set (S.right.obj.obj (op U)))) (K : Type u) [Preorder K] [IsDirected K (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty K] (E : K ⥤ X.Modules) (hE : ∀ k : K, (E.obj k).IsQuasicoherent) (ε : E ⟶ (Functor.const K).obj J) (hε : IsColimit (Cocone.mk J ε)) : ∃ (F : K ⥤ QuasiCoherentAlgebra X) (c : Cocone F) (q : (Functor.const K).obj S ⟶ F ⋙ (X.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra).ι) (p : S ⟶ c.pt.obj), (∀ (k : K) (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → Function.Surjective ((q.app k).right.hom.app (op U)) ∧ RingHom.ker ((q.app k).right.hom.app (op U)).hom = Ideal.span (Set.range ((ε.app k ≫ j).app U) : Set (S.right.obj.obj (op U)))) ∧ (∀ k : K, q.app k ≫ (c.ι.app k).hom = p) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit ((X.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra).ι.mapCocone c)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → Function.Surjective (p.right.hom.app (op U)) ∧ RingHom.ker (p.right.hom.app (op U)).hom = L U ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (((evaluation X.Opensᵒᵖ CommRingCat).obj (op U)).mapCocone ((sheafToPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat).mapCocone ((Under.forget X.sheaf).mapCocone ((X.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra).ι.mapCocone c))))))
